[Environment overview](../../overview.md) · [Code changes](02_code_changes.md) · [Findings and your notes](03_findings.md)

Review status: **targeted controller review and selected trace checks; full trace annotation pending**. Start with the table, then open an event below for its exact message, command and output.

Event IDs preserve raw stream positions: E0401 means source line 401. Gaps are normal; started/update records are retained in the raw source, not duplicated as completed actions. Boundaries and unfinished tools are shown. For Claude, B01/B02 suffixes distinguish multiple content blocks on one line; the turn column counts session initializations, not model inference turns.

Claude tools are placed at their response line, with request lines retained. A returned tool can launch a background job; it is not necessarily a finished experiment. Helper rows retain their parent identity. Empty thinking and routine progress remain in the raw stream and [coverage ledger](evidence/stream_coverage.json). No hidden reasoning is reconstructed.

**Reading rule:** arrows and adjacent rows mean recorded order, not proof of causation. For asynchronous calls, inspect the start line as well as completion. An exit code of zero is not evidence that robot tests passed. Automated tags are navigation aids, not ACT*ONOMY or decision-making labels.

Evidence: [task](evidence/task.md), [configuration](evidence/config.yaml), [raw stream](evidence/stream.jsonl), [manifest](evidence/manifest.json). 298 normalized messages/tool returns; 34 saved commits in HEAD ancestry. These extraction counts are not counts of independent decisions or finished tests.

class _ObjectCentricState:
    """A local mirror of relational_structs.ObjectCentricState.

    Holds ``{Object: feature ndarray}`` as ``data`` plus ``{Type: [feature names]}`` as
    ``type_features`` (both public, matching the real state) and exposes the read/write
    API a program uses. Iteration yields the objects, sorted by name for determinism.
    """

    def __init__(
        self,
        data: dict[_Object, np.ndarray],
        type_features: dict[_Type, list[str]],
    ) -> None:
        self.data = data
        self.type_features = type_features

    def __iter__(self) -> Any:
        return iter(sorted(self.data, key=lambda o: o.name))

    def get_object_names(self) -> set[str]:
        """The set of object names in this state."""
        return {o.name for o in self.data}

    def get_object_from_name(self, name: str) -> _Object:
        """The object with the given name."""
        for obj in self.data:
            if obj.name == name:
                return obj
        raise ValueError(f"No object named {name!r}")

    def get_objects(self, typ: _Type) -> list[_Object]:
        """Objects that are instances of *typ* (its subtypes included), by name."""
        return sorted(
            (o for o in self.data if o.is_instance(typ)), key=lambda o: o.name
        )

    def _feature_index(self, obj: _Object, feature: str) -> int:
        return self.type_features[obj.type].index(feature)

    def get(self, obj: _Object, feature: str) -> float:
        """Read a named feature of an object."""
        return float(self.data[obj][self._feature_index(obj, feature)])

    def set(self, obj: _Object, feature: str, value: float) -> None:
        """Write a named feature of an object in place."""
        self.data[obj][self._feature_index(obj, feature)] = value

    def vec(self, objects: Any) -> np.ndarray:
        """Concatenate the feature vectors of the given objects."""
        return (
            np.concatenate([self.data[o] for o in objects]) if objects else np.array([])
        )

    def copy(self) -> "_ObjectCentricState":
        """A deep copy of this state."""
        return _ObjectCentricState(
            {o: arr.copy() for o, arr in self.data.items()},
            {t: list(f) for t, f in self.type_features.items()},
        )

    def allclose(self, other: "_ObjectCentricState") -> bool:
        """True if *other* has the same objects with numerically-close features."""
        if self.get_object_names() != other.get_object_names():
            return False
        return all(
            np.allclose(self.data[o], other.data[other.get_object_from_name(o.name)])
            for o in self.data
        )


def _build_local_types(
    types_payload: list[dict[str, Any]],
) -> tuple[dict[str, _Type], dict[_Type, list[str]]]:
    """Rebuild local {name: _Type} and {_Type: [features]} (parents-first payload)."""
    type_by_name: dict[str, _Type] = {}
    type_features: dict[_Type, list[str]] = {}
    for entry in types_payload:
        parent = type_by_name[entry["parent"]] if entry["parent"] is not None else None
        typ = _Type(entry["name"], parent)
        type_by_name[entry["name"]] = typ
        type_features[typ] = list(entry["features"])
    return type_by_name, type_features


def _ocs_from_payload(payload: dict[str, Any]) -> _ObjectCentricState:
    """Reconstruct a local ObjectCentricState from a self-contained codec payload."""
    type_by_name, type_features = _build_local_types(payload["types"])
    data: dict[_Object, np.ndarray] = {}

Exact agent message:
```text
I looked at the image. Most of this is what I can see directly; the coordinates are rough estimates from where the known objects appear.

**View:** It's a 3D perspective view, not top-down. The camera is above and in front of the arena, on the -y side, looking toward +y. The near edge at the bottom of the image is y=-2.5 and the far edge is y=+2.5. +x is to the right of the image. The far part of the arena is foreshortened.

**Wall down the middle:**
- **Orientation and position:** It's straight and runs along y at x≈0, splitting the arena into a left half (x<0) and a right half (x>0).
- **Extent:** It reaches from the near boundary wall (y≈-2.5) to the far boundary wall (y≈+2.5) and touches both, so neither end seems to have a passage.
- **Thickness:** It's thin, about the same as the outer walls, roughly 0.05–0.1 m. Its height is also low and matches the outer walls.
- **Gaps:** I see no obvious gap. There is a faint break or joint at about image row 270, which works out to roughly y≈-1.0 to -1.3, just in front of the rover start line. It could be a seam between two wall segments, but at this resolution I can't tell if it's a real opening. If it matters, check the wall geometry in the env/XML or render a top-down view.
- **Effect:** Each rover seems to be stuck in its own half. The far end of the wall falls between the mounds at x=-0.5 and x=+0.5.

**Arena boundary:** A continuous gray wall runs around the whole 5×5 m square, with no visible openings.

**Other objects:**
- **Rovers:** At (1.0,-1.75) and (-1.0,-1.75) there are translucent glass-like cylinders, one in each half. These match the stated rover positions, so the rovers seem to be drawn as transparent cylinders.
- **Lander:** The large yellow-and-black wheeled vehicle in the near-left corner, about (-1.9,-2.0), sits where the lander should be. So the yellow vehicle is probably the lander, not a rover.
- **Mounds:** Four flat gray square pads sit at y≈2, at x≈-2, -0.5, +0.5 and +2.
- **Objectives:** Small blue upright markers sit on the mounds at x=-2, +0.5 and +2. I can't see a blue marker on the x=-0.5 mound; it may be missing or hidden.
- **Pillars:** There are about 7 dark gray vertical posts, mostly in the middle and far parts of the arena:
  - Left half: about (-1.3,0.5), (-0.9,0.2), (-2.1,-0.1).
  - Near the wall: about (-0.15,-0.5) on the left side.
  - Right half: about (0.6,-0.1) and (0.25,1.0).
  - One tall post at about (1.0,2.4) near the back wall.
  These positions are rough perspective estimates.
- **Debris:** A few small brown or black specks lie on the floor, for example near (-1.0,-0.3), (-0.9,0.7) and (-0.3,-2.0), plus a couple of dark specks near the back. They look like small rocks or decoration.
```

import numpy as np
env = make_env()
obs, info = env.reset(seed=0)
r0 = obs.get_object_from_name('rover0')
def p(o): return tuple(round(obs.get(o,f),4) for f in ['x','y','theta'])
# rover0 to the wall with fine steps
for i in range(200):
    obs,*_ = env.step(np.array([-0.01,0,0,0, 0,0,0,0],dtype=np.float32))
print('r0 min x at y=-1.75', p(r0))
# move up along wall, testing whether wall ends
xs=[]
for i in range(40):
    obs,*_ = env.step(np.array([0,0.1,0,0, 0,0,0,0],dtype=np.float32))
    # try to move left
    b=obs.get(r0,'x')
    obs,*_ = env.step(np.array([-0.05,0,0,0, 0,0,0,0],dtype=np.float32))
    xs.append((round(obs.get(r0,'y'),2), round(obs.get(r0,'x'),3)))
print(xs)
env.close()
"""Client for the black-box environment server.

This file is copied into the agent sandbox. Import it in test and
exploration scripts to interact with the environment without access to its
source code::

    from env_client import make_env

    env = make_env()
    obs, info = env.reset(seed=0)
    obs, reward, terminated, truncated, info = env.step(action)
    state = env.get_state()
    env.set_state(state)
    primitives = env.make_primitives()  # same dict the eval harness passes
    env.close()

Each call to ``make_env()`` creates a fresh, independent environment
instance on the server, so parallel test scripts are safe.

The list above is the legacy blackbox interface. When ``env_spaces.json`` has
``"strict": true``, only reset, step, rendering, close, and generic space metadata
are supported; the host server rejects every other helper command independently.

NOTE: ``approach.py`` must NOT import this module. It is evaluated by a
separate harness that calls it directly with real observations; this client
is only for test and exploration scripts.

This module must stay importable with only the standard library and numpy.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import importlib
import json
import socket
import sys
from pathlib import Path
from typing import Any

import numpy as np

"""Client for the black-box environment server.

This file is copied into the agent sandbox. Import it in test and
exploration scripts to interact with the environment without access to its
source code::

    from env_client import make_env

    env = make_env()
    obs, info = env.reset(seed=0)
    obs, reward, terminated, truncated, info = env.step(action)
    state = env.get_state()
    env.set_state(state)
    primitives = env.make_primitives()  # same dict the eval harness passes
    env.close()

Each call to ``make_env()`` creates a fresh, independent environment
instance on the server, so parallel test scripts are safe.

The list above is the legacy blackbox interface. When ``env_spaces.json`` has
``"strict": true``, only reset, step, rendering, close, and generic space metadata
are supported; the host server rejects every other helper command independently.

NOTE: ``approach.py`` must NOT import this module. It is evaluated by a
separate harness that calls it directly with real observations; this client
is only for test and exploration scripts.

This module must stay importable with only the standard library and numpy.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import importlib
import json
import socket
import sys
from pathlib import Path
from typing import Any

import numpy as np

_METADATA_PATH = Path(__file__).resolve().parent / "env_spaces.json"
_NDARRAY_TAG = "__ndarray__"
_HANDLE_TAG = "__handle__"
_MODULE_TAG = "__module__"
_SET_TAG = "__set__"
_OCS_TAG = "__ocs__"


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Local ObjectCentricState mirror
#
# A variable-count env hands the program an ObjectCentricState. This sandbox module
# must stay importable with only the standard library and numpy, so rather than import
# relational_structs it reconstructs a faithful local mirror from the self-contained
# codec payload (which embeds the type hierarchy). The mirror implements the subset of
# the ObjectCentricState API a generated program uses, with the same semantics -- most
# importantly `is_instance` over the ancestor chain and `get(obj, feature)` by name --
# so a program tested here behaves as it will at eval against the real state.
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
from env_client import make_env
import numpy as np
env = make_env()
obs, info = env.reset(seed=0)
r0 = obs.get_object_from_name('rover0'); r1=obs.get_object_from_name('rover1')
def p(o): return tuple(round(obs.get(o,f),3) for f in ['x','y','theta','store_full','calibrated','at_home'])
# move rover0 -x, rover1 nothing
for i in range(8):
    obs,r,te,tr,inf = env.step(np.array([-0.2,0,0,0, 0,0,0,0],dtype=np.float32))
    print(i,p(r0),p(r1),r,te,tr)
# try bigger than limits
obs,r,te,tr,inf = env.step(np.array([0,0.5,0,0, 0,0,0,0],dtype=np.float32)); print('big',p(r0))
obs,r,te,tr,inf = env.step(np.array([0,0,0.4,0, 0,0,0,0],dtype=np.float32)); print('rot',p(r0))
# move rover1 +y up the left side
for i in range(25):
    obs,r,te,tr,inf = env.step(np.array([0,0,0,0, 0,0.2,0,0],dtype=np.float32))
print('r1 after up',p(r1))
env.close()

- Action per rover: [dx(+-0.2), dy(+-0.2), dtheta(+-0.4), selector]. Selector band centres: sample=-0.8333, calibrate=-0.5, image=-0.1667, noop=0.1667, send=0.5, drop=0.8333. (0 = noop)
- Rover starts: rover0 (1.0,-1.75,theta=pi), rover1 (-1.0,-1.75,theta=0). Lander fixed (-1.9,-2.0).
- Mounds: obstacles with half_x=0.25 at (+-2,2),(+-0.5,2), z small. Objectives sit on mounds (z=0.2). Pillars: half 0.05x0.05, height 0.4.

- Arena is 5m square (approx -2.5..2.5).

cd /sandbox; cat > probe_col_lib.py <<'EOF'
from env_client import make_env
import numpy as np
class R:
    def __init__(self, seed=0):
        self.env=make_env(); self.obs,_=self.env.reset(seed=seed)
    def pos(self,i):
        o=self.obs.get_object_from_name(f'rover{i}')
        return np.array([self.obs.get(o,'x'),self.obs.get(o,'y'),self.obs.get(o,'theta')],float)
    def step(self,i,dx=0,dy=0,dth=0):
        a=np.zeros(8,np.float32); a[4*i:4*i+3]=[dx,dy,dth]
        self.obs,*_=self.env.step(a)
        return self.pos(i)
    def goto(self,i,x,y,maxit=200):
        for _ in range(maxit):
            p=self.pos(i); d=np.array([x,y])-p[:2]
            if np.linalg.norm(d)<1e-6: return True
            d=np.clip(d,-0.2,0.2)
            q=self.step(i,*d)
            if np.allclose(q[:2],p[:2]): return False
        return False
    def path(self,i,pts):
        for (x,y) in pts:
            if not self.goto(i,x,y): print('blocked going to',(x,y),'at',self.pos(i)); return False
        return True
    def push(self,i,ux,uy,step=0.005,maxit=2000):
        """move in direction (ux,uy) with given step until blocked; return last pos"""
        u=np.array([ux,uy],float); u/=np.linalg.norm(u)
        # coarse
        for s in [0.05,step]:
            for _ in range(maxit):
                p=self.pos(i); q=self.step(i,*(u*s))
                if np.allclose(q[:2],p[:2],atol=1e-9): break
        # finer
        for s in [0.001]:
            for _ in range(maxit):
                p=self.pos(i); q=self.step(i,*(u*s))
                if np.allclose(q[:2],p[:2],atol=1e-9): break
        return self.pos(i)
    def obst(self):
        out=[]
        for o in self.obs:
            if o.type.name=='obstacle':
                out.append((o.name,self.obs.get(o,'x'),self.obs.get(o,'y'),self.obs.get(o,'half_x')))
        return out
EOF

from env_client import make_env
import numpy as np, math
SEL={'sample':-0.8333,'cal':-0.5,'img':-0.1667,'noop':0.0,'send':0.5,'drop':0.8333}
class E:
    def __init__(s,seed):
        s.env=make_env(); s.obs,_=s.env.reset(seed=seed); s.seed=seed
    def r(s,i): return s.obs.get_object_from_name('rover%d'%i)
    def rs(s,i):
        o=s.r(i); return {f:s.obs.get(o,f) for f in ['x','y','theta','store_full','calibrated','at_home']}
    def objs(s):
        out={}
        for o in s.obs:
            if o.type.name=='objective':
                out[o.name]={f:s.obs.get(o,f) for f in ['x','y','z','have_image_rover0','have_image_rover1','received_image']}
        return out
    def step(s,i,dx=0,dy=0,dth=0,sel='noop',other=None):
        a=np.zeros(8,np.float32)
        a[4*i:4*i+4]=[dx,dy,dth,SEL[sel]]
        if other is not None: a[4*(1-i):4*(1-i)+4]=other
        s.obs,rew,te,tr,inf=s.env.step(a); return rew
    def goto(s,i,x,y,tol=1e-4,maxit=200):
        for _ in range(maxit):
            st=s.rs(i); ex=x-st['x']; ey=y-st['y']
            if abs(ex)<tol and abs(ey)<tol: return True
            dx=float(np.clip(ex,-0.2,0.2)); dy=float(np.clip(ey,-0.2,0.2))
            s.step(i,dx,dy)
            st2=s.rs(i)
            if abs(st2['x']-st['x'])<1e-9 and abs(st2['y']-st['y'])<1e-9:
                return False
        return False
    def path(s,i,pts):
        for p in pts:
            if not s.goto(i,*p): return False
        return True
    def turn(s,i,th,maxit=50):
        for _ in range(maxit):
            e=(th-s.rs(i)['theta']+math.pi)%(2*math.pi)-math.pi
            if abs(e)<1e-5: return
            s.step(i,0,0,float(np.clip(e,-0.4,0.4)))
    def close(s): s.env.close()

    def act(s,k,mv=(0,0,0),sel=0.0):

            mx,my=np.clip(dx,-0.2,0.2),np.clip(dy,-0.2,0.2)

        return False

            if abs(d)<1e-4: return

    def flags(s):

                out[o.name]=s.feats(o.name)
        return out
def diff(a,b):

import heapq
def plan(e,k,goal,clr=0.27,res=0.05):
    obs=[]
    for o in e.obs:
        if o.type.name=='obstacle':
            n=o.name; obs.append((e.g(n,'x'),e.g(n,'y'),e.g(n,'half_x'),e.g(n,'half_y')))
    def free(x,y):
        if abs(x)>2.5-0.2 or abs(y)>2.5-0.2: return False
        if k==0 and x<0.24: return False
        if k==1 and x>-0.24: return False
        for ox,oy,hx,hy in obs:
            if abs(x-ox)<hx+clr and abs(y-oy)<hy+clr: return False
        return True
    st=e.pose(k)[:2]
    toi=lambda p:(int(round(p[0]/res)),int(round(p[1]/res)))
    s=toi(st); g=toi(goal)
    pq=[(0,s)]; came={s:None}; cost={s:0}
    while pq:
        _,c=heapq.heappop(pq)
        if c==g: break
        for dx in (-1,0,1):
            for dy in (-1,0,1):
                if dx==dy==0: continue
                n=(c[0]+dx,c[1]+dy)
                if not free(n[0]*res,n[1]*res) and n!=g: continue
                nc=cost[c]+np.hypot(dx,dy)
                if n not in cost or nc<cost[n]:
                    cost[n]=nc; came[n]=c; heapq.heappush(pq,(nc+np.hypot(n[0]-g[0],n[1]-g[1]),n))
    if g not in came: return None
    path=[]; c=g
    while c: path.append((c[0]*res,c[1]*res)); c=came[c]
    return path[::-1]
def nav(e,k,goal,clr=0.27):
    path=plan(e,k,goal,clr)
    if path is None: return False
    # compress: follow points
    for p in path[1:]:
        e.goto(k,*p,maxit=5)
    return e.goto(k,*goal,maxit=20)
EOF

grep -n "wp" probe_send_d.py; timeout 300 /opt/robocode-strict/bin/python probe_send_d.py -1.25 2.4

cd /sandbox; cat > probe_col_rays.py <<'EOF'
from probe_col_lib import R
import numpy as np, sys
c=np.array([0.654,-0.199]); RAD=0.42
def approach(r,i,target,tol=1e-4):
    step=0.2
    while step>tol:
        p=r.pos(i)[:2]; d=target-p; n=np.linalg.norm(d)
        if n<1e-6: break
        s=min(step,n); q=r.step(i,*(d/n*s))[:2]
        if np.allclose(q,p,atol=1e-9): step/=2
    return r.pos(i)
def run(dths,label):
    r=R(0)
    r.path(0,[(1.0,-1.0),(c[0]+RAD,c[1])])
    for d in dths: r.step(0,0,0,d)
    th=r.pos(0)[2]
    res=[]
    for k in range(0,72):
        a=np.deg2rad(k*5)
        S=c+RAD*np.array([np.cos(a),np.sin(a)])
        if not r.goto(0,*S): print('nav fail',k,r.pos(0)); break
        p=approach(r,0,c)
        rel=p[:2]-c
        res.append((k*5,rel[0],rel[1]))
        r.goto(0,*S)
    print(label,'theta=%.4f'%th)
    for a,x,y in res: print('%3d %.4f %.4f  r=%.4f'%(a,x,y,np.hypot(x,y)))
    r.env.close()
mode=sys.argv[1]
if mode=='0': run([],'th=pi')
if mode=='1': run([0.4],'th=pi+0.4')
if mode=='2': run([0.4,0.4,0.4,0.37079633],'th=pi/2 ish')
EOF
for m in 0 1 2; do /opt/robocode-strict/bin/python probe_col_rays.py $m > probe_col_rays_$m.txt & done; wait; cat probe_col_rays_0.txt | head -80

cat > probe_vis_e.py <<'EOF'
from probe_vis_lib import *
A,B,D=-0.087,-0.0125,1.99758
def pred_t(o,u,th):
    # find t s.t. camera at o + t*u (rover center) dist = D
    lo,hi=0.5,3.0
    for _ in range(60):
        t=(lo+hi)/2; cx=o[0]+t*u[0]+A*math.cos(th)-B*math.sin(th); cy=o[1]+t*u[1]+A*math.sin(th)+B*math.cos(th)
        if math.hypot(cx-o[0],cy-o[1])<=D: lo=t
        else: hi=t
    return lo
for ang,th in [(-90,0.3),(-70,1.2),(-55,-2.0),(-40,2.8)]:
    e=E(1)
    ob=e.objs()['objective1']; o=(ob['x'],ob['y'])
    u=(math.cos(math.radians(ang)),math.sin(math.radians(ang)))
    p0=(o[0]+2.3*u[0],o[1]+2.3*u[1])
    ok=e.path(1,[(-1.0,-1.0),(p0[0],-1.0),p0]); 
    e.turn(1,th); th=e.rs(1)['theta']
    lo,hi=1.8,2.3
    for it in range(16):
        t=(lo+hi)/2
        e.goto(1,o[0]+t*u[0],o[1]+t*u[1],tol=1e-7)
        e.step(1,0,0,0,'cal'); c=e.rs(1)['calibrated']; e.step(1,0,0,0,'img')
        if c: hi=t
        else: lo=t
    # note: here lo= fails side? visible when t small
    print('ang',ang,'th=%.3f ok=%s measured t*=%.5f predicted %.5f'%(th,ok,hi,pred_t(o,u,th)))
    e.close()
EOF

        s=min(step,n); q=r.step(i,*(d/n*s))[:2]
        if np.allclose(q,p,atol=1e-9): step/=2
    return r.pos(i)
def rot(r,i,tot):
    while abs(tot)>1e-9:

for dth in [0,0.4,np.pi/4,np.pi/2,1.0]:

cat > probe_vis_geo.py <<'EOF'
import math, numpy as np
A,B,D=-0.087,-0.0125,1.99758
def cam(x,y,th): return (x+A*math.cos(th)-B*math.sin(th), y+A*math.sin(th)+B*math.cos(th))
def seg_box_dist(p,q,c,h):
    # distance between segment pq and axis-aligned box center c half h (0 if intersect), via dense sampling + exact
    best=1e9
    for t in np.linspace(0,1,4001):
        x=p[0]+t*(q[0]-p[0]); y=p[1]+t*(q[1]-p[1])
        dx=max(abs(x-c[0])-h[0],0); dy=max(abs(y-c[1])-h[1],0)
        # signed penetration
        if dx==0 and dy==0: d=-min(h[0]-abs(x-c[0]),h[1]-abs(y-c[1]))
        else: d=math.hypot(dx,dy)
        best=min(best,d)
    return best
def seg_pt_dist(p,q,c):
    px,py=q[0]-p[0],q[1]-p[1]; t=((c[0]-p[0])*px+(c[1]-p[1])*py)/(px*px+py*py); t=min(1,max(0,t))
    return math.hypot(p[0]+t*px-c[0],p[1]+t*py-c[1])
EOF
cat > probe_vis_f.py <<'EOF'
from probe_vis_lib import *
from probe_vis_geo import *
e=E(1)
ob=e.objs()['objective1']; o=(ob['x'],ob['y'])
pil=(-1.002,0.435)

    if o_.name=='obstacle8': pil=(e.obs.get(o_,'x'),e.obs.get(o_,'y'))
print('pillar',pil)
e.path(1,[(-1.0,-1.0),(-0.9,-1.0),(-0.9,0.0)])
e.turn(1,0.0)
t=1.75
for k in range(41):
    ang=-58+k*0.15
    u=(math.cos(math.radians(ang)),math.sin(math.radians(ang)))
    p=(o[0]+t*u[0],o[1]+t*u[1])
    ok=e.goto(1,*p,tol=1e-7)
    st=e.rs(1)
    e.step(1,0,0,0,'cal'); c=e.rs(1)['calibrated']; e.step(1,0,0,0,'img')
    C=cam(st['x'],st['y'],st['theta'])
    print('ang=%.2f ok=%d vis=%d boxdist=%.4f ctrdist=%.4f ctrdist_center=%.4f'%(ang,ok,c,seg_box_dist(C,o,pil,(0.05,0.05)),seg_pt_dist(C,o,pil),seg_pt_dist((st['x'],st['y']),o,pil)))
EOF

from probe_col_bounds import approach, rot
import numpy as np, sys
c=np.array([-1.9,-2.0]); RAD=1.0
r=R(3)  # seed 3: check obstacles
print([o for o in r.obst() if o[1]<0 and o[2]<0 and o[3]<0.1])
rot(r,1,float(sys.argv[1]))
r.goto(1,-1.0,-1.2)
for k in range(-30,125,5):
    a=np.deg2rad(k); S=c+RAD*np.array([np.cos(a),np.sin(a)])
    S=np.clip(S,-2.27,-0.23)
    if not r.goto(1,-1.0,-1.2) or not r.goto(1,*S): print(k,'nav fail',r.pos(1)); continue
    p=approach(r,1,c,tol=2e-4); rel=p[:2]-c
    print('%4d rel %.4f %.4f  r=%.4f th=%.3f'%(k,rel[0],rel[1],np.hypot(*rel),p[2]))
EOF

Exact agent message:
```text
I measured all seven items. The main finding is that the rover's footprint changes depending on what it is hitting, so a single radius doesn't describe it. Values below were found by bisection to about 1e-4 m (lander scan about 2e-4). Positions are rover centre coordinates. There is no `set_state` in strict mode, so every probe drives the rover there.

**7. Motion frame.** Moves are in the world frame, whatever the heading. Rover0 at theta=pi with dx=+0.2 moves +x, and moves are exact: (0.123, -0.077) gives exactly that change. Values are clipped to ±0.2 / ±0.4. A move into collision is rejected entirely, not clamped. Rotations are also collision-checked: a rotation that would cause a collision is rejected, so turning next to a pillar can fail.

**6. Collision timing.** Only the end position is checked, not the path. A diagonal step of (-0.17, +0.17) went straight through a pillar's corner region with both ends free. Jumping fully over a pillar or the wall is still impossible, because the blocked zone is about 0.45 m wide and a step is at most 0.283 m.

**1. Rover shape.** The footprint depends on which obstacle it hits:
- **Pillars (tall boxes, half 0.05):** not a circle; heading matters and the shape is lumpy. I scanned rays at 1–5° spacing at headings pi, pi+0.4 and about pi/2. Distance from the rover centre to the pillar box at contact ranged from **0.167 to 0.2375**. At theta=pi the body reaches about 0.183 forward, 0.195 back and 0.18 to each side, with small bumps and cut-off corners.
  - Head-on approaches stop with the centre 0.233 from the pillar centre on the x axis.
  - **Recommended model: a circle of radius 0.24 against the pillar box.** This is safe at any heading, including while turning.
- **Mounds (low, half 0.25):** they are obstacles. Here the rover behaves as a circle of radius **0.177** against the mound box, at any heading and any approach direction. Contact is at a centre distance of 0.427 from the mound centre along each axis.
- **Walls (arena edge and middle wall):** circle of radius **0.2271**, independent of heading.

**2. Arena bounds (both rovers, any heading).** |x| ≤ 2.2729 and |y| ≤ 2.2729.

**3. Middle wall.** Rover0 x ≥ +0.2271 and rover1 x ≤ -0.2271, exactly, at every heading. I slid each rover along the wall every 0.05 in y from -2.27 to 1.55 over seeds 0–3, and every reachable y was blocked at ±0.2271. **There are no gaps.** Above y≈1.57 the mounds at (±0.5, 2) keep the rovers away from the wall anyway. Pillars sitting near the wall (x of about 0.24–0.34, as in seed 1) can wall off whole stretches, which looks like a dead-end pocket for the planner.

**4. Lander at (-1.9, -2.0).** It is a large obstacle. The zone rover1's centre cannot enter, relative to the lander centre:
- Heading 0: blocked if rel x < 0.690 and rel y < 0.521. The corner is cut off, passing through (0.690, 0.398), (0.651, 0.456), (0.590, 0.495), (0.514, 0.514) and (0.436, 0.520).
- Heading pi/2: rel x < 0.674 and rel y < 0.530.
- **Safe planner rule: keep the rover centre at x ≥ -1.205 or y ≥ -1.465.** Because the lander sits in the corner, nothing can pass behind it.

**5. Rover vs rover.** This can't happen: both rovers sat against the wall at the same y at the same time (±0.2271, -1.75), with centres 0.454 apart.

The probe scripts are in /sandbox as probe_col_*.py. The shared helper is probe_col_lib.py, and probe_col_bounds.py provides `approach` (bisection) and `rot`. Raw ray scans are in probe_col_rays_*.txt, probe_col_f_*.txt, probe_col_lander_*.txt and probe_col_m_*.txt.
```

cat > probe_vis_model.py <<'EOF'
import math, json, numpy as np
def seg_box_hit(p,q,lo,hi):
    # slab test for 3D segment p->q vs box [lo,hi]
    t0,t1=0.0,1.0
    for k in range(len(p)):
        d=q[k]-p[k]
        if abs(d)<1e-12:
            if p[k]<lo[k] or p[k]>hi[k]: return False
        else:
            a=(lo[k]-p[k])/d; b=(hi[k]-p[k])/d
            if a>b: a,b=b,a
            t0=max(t0,a); t1=min(t1,b)
            if t0>t1: return False
    return True
def visible(rx,ry,th,obj,obstacles,a=-0.087,b=-0.0125,zc=None,D=1.99758,infl=0.0,dim3=True,ozoff=0.0,skip_own=True):
    cx=rx+a*math.cos(th)-b*math.sin(th); cy=ry+a*math.sin(th)+b*math.cos(th)
    ox,oy,oz=obj
    if math.hypot(ox-cx,oy-cy)>D: return False
    for (x,y,z,hx,hy,hz) in obstacles:
        if skip_own and abs(x-ox)<=hx and abs(y-oy)<=hy: continue
        if dim3:
            if seg_box_hit((cx,cy,zc),(ox,oy,oz+ozoff),(x-hx-infl,y-hy-infl,z-hz),(x+hx+infl,y+hy+infl,z+hz)): return False
        else:
            if seg_box_hit((cx,cy),(ox,oy),(x-hx-infl,y-hy-infl),(x+hx+infl,y+hy+infl)): return False
    return True
EOF
cat > probe_vis_fit2.py <<'EOF'
import sys, json, math
from probe_vis_model import *
from probe_vis_lib import E
files=sys.argv[1:]
sets=[]
for f in files:
    d=json.load(open(f)); e=E(d['seed'])
    ob=e.objs()[d['obj']]; obj=(ob['x'],ob['y'],ob['z'])
    obs=[]
    for o in e.obs:
        if o.type.name=='obstacle': obs.append(tuple(e.obs.get(o,k) for k in ['x','y','z','half_x','half_y','half_z']))
    e.close(); sets.append((obj,obs,d['data']))
def score(**kw):
    m=0;n=0
    for obj,obs,data in sets:
        for x,y,th,c in data:
            n+=1; m+= (visible(x,y,th,obj,obs,**kw)!=bool(c))
    return m,n
print('2D cam',score(dim3=False))
print('2D center',score(dim3=False,a=0,b=0))
for zc in [0.2,0.3,0.4,0.45,0.5,0.52,0.53,0.54,0.55,0.56,0.58,0.6,0.7]:
    print('3D zc',zc,score(zc=zc), 'center', score(zc=zc,a=0,b=0))

<a id="E0482"></a>
### E0482 · Message

Source line 482; turn 1; start line not saved/not applicable.

[Previous](#E0479) · [Next](#E0485)

Actor: helper: Probe send/sample/termination. Parent tool: `toolu_015ffPMG5kK5aVDxx9AEiGmU`. Timestamp: 2026-10-01T08:53:25.884Z.

Exact agent message:
```text
Rover0 can send. The hidden x=0 wall does not block line of sight: rover0 sent successfully from (0.24,-2.0), (0.24,0.25), (1.5,-1.0) and (1.0,-2.0). So rover0 can sample and image things on the right half and send them itself.

**1. Send (selector 0.5)**
- **Range:** the 2D distance from rover center to lander center (-1.9,-2.0) must be within 4.0. It worked at 3.9994 and failed at 4.019.
- **Occlusion:** pillars and the other rover block the line to the lander. Rover1 facing the lander at (-1.65,-1.1) failed because pillar10 is in the way; at (-1.4,-1.1) with nothing in the way it worked. Rover0 at (1.5,-1.0) facing pi failed while rover1 sat at home in the line, and worked once rover1 moved away.
- **Heading matters, but only when something is in the way.** With a clear line, every heading works. With a blocked line, send still works if the lander is behind the rover. Test case: rover0 at (1.0,-2.0), rover1 parked at (-0.6,-2.0) on the line, so the lander is at bearing pi. Send worked at theta -1.0, 0, 0.5, 1.0, 1.3 and failed at 1.57, 2.0, 2.5, pi, -2.0. That puts the cutoff near 90° between heading and lander direction. My guess is the sight line starts at the front of the rover and passes through its own body. Whatever the cause, **facing away from the lander before sending gets past occluders.**
- **Effects:** one send transfers everything the rover holds at once (a soil analysis and an image both arrived from a single send). It sets `received_analysis=1` on samples and `received_image=1` on objectives. `analyzed_roverK` and `have_image_roverK` stay at 1, and the store is not touched. Nothing else seems to be required: send worked with a full store too.

**2. Sample (-0.8333) and drop (0.8333)**
- **Range:** rover center to sample (x,y) distance about 0.25. It worked at 0.245 and failed at 0.250. Heading doesn't matter (worked facing toward, away and sideways).
- **Effects:** sets `store_full=1` and `analyzed_roverK=1`. The sample object stays where it is, and the same sample can be sampled again after a drop.
- **Full store:** sampling does nothing.
- **Drop:** sets `store_full=0`, does nothing on an empty store, and leaves `analyzed` flags alone.
- **Alternating:** sample and drop can alternate on consecutive steps without moving.
- **Selector band:** -1.0, -0.7 and -0.67 all sample; -0.66 does not, so sample covers roughly [-1, -0.667].
- **Nearest sample when two are in range:** not tested; I didn't find a layout with two samples within 0.25.

**3. Termination**
- **Goal reached:** `terminated=True` on the step the goal becomes true. Confirmed on seed 1 (both rovers) and seed 27, where rover0 contributed the rock from the right half.
- Only one rock and one soil analysis needed to arrive; the other samples did not. I didn't test whether every objective's image is required, because in both runs all objectives were imaged.
- **Store must be empty:** with everything received and both rovers home but rover0 still holding a sample, there was no termination. It came on the step after the drop.
- **Rewards and after termination:** reward is -1 every step with no bonus. Stepping after termination keeps returning `terminated=True`.
- **No truncation from the env:** at steps 1000–1005, `truncated` was still False, so any 1000-step cap must come from the harness.
- **at_home tolerance:** the start pose (rover1 (-1,-1.75,0), rover0 (1,-1.75,pi)) counts as home if the distance is below 0.25 (0.24 yes, 0.25 no, both along an axis and diagonally) and the heading is within about 0.4 rad. At exactly 0.4 one run said yes and another said no, so treat 0.4 as the edge; aim for under 0.35.
- **Rover1 alone:** I couldn't finish a rover1-only goal. On seed 27 the only rock on the left is sample0 at (-1.79,-2.24), next to the lander, and rover1 never got within 0.25 of it (the lander seems to be solid).
- **Calibrate and image, incidentally:** calibrate sets `calibrated=1`; image then sets `have_image_roverK` and clears `calibrated`. From (-1.4,1.3) and (-1.5,1.5) this worked at any heading.

**4. Moving and acting in the same step:** the move happens first, then the action, judged at the new position. Moving 0.2 into range and sampling in one step succeeded; moving out of range and sampling in one step failed. Per NOTES, a blocked move leaves the rover in place and the action still runs there.

Also: dx and dy are in world coordinates, not relative to heading.

The probe scripts are `/sandbox/probe_send_*.py` (a–u). The shared helper `/sandbox/probe_send_lib.py` has a simple path planner (`nav`) that keeps 0.27 clear of obstacles.
```

On seed 27 the only rock on the left is sample0 at (-1.79,-2.24), next to the lander, and rover1 never got within 0.25 of it (the lander seems to be solid).\n- **Calibrate and image, incidentally:** calibrate sets `calibrated=1`; image then sets `have_image_roverK` and clears `calibrated`. From (-1.4,1.3) and (-1.5,1.5) this worked at any heading.\n\n**4. Moving and acting in the same step:** the move happens first, then the action, judged at the new position. Moving 0.2 into range and sampling in one step succeeded; moving out of range and sampling in one step failed. Per NOTES, a blocked move leaves the rover in place and the action still runs there.\n\nAlso: dx and dy are in world coordinates, not relative to heading.\n\nThe probe scripts are `/sandbox/probe_send_*.py` (a–u).     e.close(); sets.append((obj,obs,d['data']))
def vis(x,y,th,obj,obs,a,b,thr,origin_cam):
    cx=x+a*math.cos(th)-b*math.sin(th); cy=y+a*math.sin(th)+b*math.cos(th)

            rel=math.atan2(py-oy,px-ox)-th; rel=(rel+math.pi)%(2*math.pi)-math.pi

import json, math, glob
import numpy as np
from probe_vis_model import seg_box_hit
from probe_vis_lib import E
e=E(4); ob=e.objs()['objective2']; obj=(ob['x'],ob['y'])
obs=[tuple(e.obs.get(o,k) for k in ['x','y','z','half_x','half_y','half_z']) for o in e.obs if o.type.name=='obstacle']; e.close()
data=json.load(open('probe_vis_d1.json'))['data']
for f in glob.glob('probe_vis_j_*_0.75.json')+glob.glob('probe_vis_n_*.json'): data+=json.load(open(f))
HOLES=[(-79.5,-74),(-57.5,-53),(48,52.5),(70,76.5)]
def rel(x,y,th):
    r=math.degrees(math.atan2(obj[1]-y,obj[0]-x)-th); return (r+180)%360-180
def vis(x,y,th,a,b,infl,thr=97.5,holes=True):
    r=rel(x,y,th)
    if abs(r)>thr: return True
    if holes and any(lo<=r<=hi for lo,hi in HOLES): return True
    cx=x+a*math.cos(th)-b*math.sin(th); cy=y+a*math.sin(th)+b*math.cos(th)
    for (px,py,pz,hx,hy,hz) in obs:
        if abs(px-obj[0])<=hx and abs(py-obj[1])<=hy: continue
        if seg_box_hit((cx,cy),obj,(px-hx-infl,py-hy-infl),(px+hx+infl,py+hy+infl)): return False
    return True
print(len(data))
res=[]
for a in np.arange(-0.16,0.061,0.02):
    for b in np.arange(-0.06,0.061,0.02):
        for infl in [0,0.01,0.02,0.03]:
            res.append((sum(vis(x,y,th,a,b,infl)!=bool(c) for x,y,th,c in data),round(a,3),round(b,3),infl))
res.sort(); print(res[:8])
m,a,b,infl=res[0]
mm=[(round(math.degrees(th)),round(x,3),round(y,3),round(rel(x,y,th),1),c) for x,y,th,c in data if vis(x,y,th,a,b,infl)!=bool(c)]
print(mm[:60])

### E0600 · Message

[Previous](#E0598) · [Next](#E0603)

Actor: helper: Probe objective visibility. Parent tool: `toolu_012S4fk7yaqqweG86LUDvXsc`. Timestamp: 2026-10-01T09:02:17.747Z.

Exact agent message:
````text
I've pinned down range, timing, image target choice, the wall and the mounds precisely. Pillar occlusion is only modelled empirically: my best model gets about 1% of 3,896 recorded tests wrong (40 mismatches, all at shadow edges). Seeds used were 0–5 and both rovers; the visibility check is the same for calibrate and image.

**1. Range (2D, measured from an offset camera point)**
- Visibility is measured from a camera point, not the rover centre: `cam = (x,y) + R(theta)·(-0.087, -0.0125)`, i.e. 0.087 behind the centre and 0.0125 to the right.
- Visible requires `hypot(obj.xy - cam) <= 1.9976`. I fitted this on 8 headings with residuals of 1e-5, then confirmed it on rover1 along other rays: predicted 1.95835 / 1.91960, measured 1.95836 / 1.91960.
- 1.9976 is what you get from a 3D distance of 2.0 with about 0.098 of height difference. All objectives sit at z=0.201, so I can't tell 2D from 3D. In practice, rover-centre distance ≤ about 1.88 is always safe.

**2. Heading**
- There is no field-of-view limit for range: at about 0.92 m, every one of 16 headings calibrated.
- Heading does matter for occlusion (next item).

**3. Occlusion**
- **Pillars block, but only when the objective is roughly in front of the rover.** Let `rel = bearing(rover centre → objective) - theta`. If |rel| > about 97–98°, pillars are ignored entirely. Calibrate and image both succeed from deep inside a pillar's shadow. This held on seed 4 (3 positions, 1° sweeps) and seed 2 (rover0, different pillar).
- When |rel| < 97°, the best fit is a 2D segment test from a camera point offset about (-0.08, 0) to the objective's (x,y), against the pillar boxes inflated by about 0.01.
- There are also narrow "see-through" windows about 4–6° wide, at roughly rel ∈ [73.5,80], [52.5,58], [-53.5,-48] and [-77.5,-70]. They repeat consistently across positions and seeds but look like an implementation artifact. Don't rely on them.
- **Mounds don't block.** The target's own mound doesn't, and on seed 5 rover0 at (1.0,2.0), facing straight at it, saw the objective on the (-0.5,2) mound through the (0.5,2) mound. Other layouts where a mound could sit in between are mostly unreachable anyway.
- **Not tested:** whether samples, other objectives or the other rover block the view.

**4. Image and calibrate semantics**
- Visibility is checked after the same step's motion is applied. Calibrate or image combined with a move works, and uses the new position.
- `calibrated` persists through noops, moves and rotations until a successful image. Calibrating at a visible spot and imaging later from elsewhere works, as long as some objective is visible at image time.
- Image without calibration does nothing.
- Image with nothing visible does nothing and keeps `calibrated`=1.
- Image photographs the nearest visible objective this rover hasn't imaged yet. On seed 0 it picked the 0.61 m objective over the 1.31 m one, then the other on the next try.
- If every visible objective is already imaged by this rover, image still uses up the calibration and changes nothing.
- Calibrate succeeds if any objective is in view, even ones already imaged.
- Calibrate and image both return reward -1 per step, like other steps.

**5. Hidden wall**
- The wall does not block the view. On seed 5, rover0 at (0.25,1.2) and (0.25,1.45) imaged objective1 at (-0.41,1.94), at all four headings tried, including facing it.
- So each rover can image objectives on the other side within range, mainly the ones on the ±0.5 mounds.

**Visibility rule (empirical):**
```
visible = dist2D(cam, obj) <= 1.9976
          and (|wrap(bearing_center_to_obj - theta)| > ~98deg
               or segment(cam', obj) misses every pillar box inflated by ~0.01)
```
Here `cam` uses offset (-0.087, -0.0125) and `cam'` uses about (-0.08, 0). The wall and mounds are ignored. Practical tip: turn the rover to face away from the objective (|rel| ≥ about 110°) and the line-of-sight check is skipped.

**Side note:** the rover body isn't circular. It got within about 0.125 of a pillar edge in one direction, and turns can be rejected near obstacles.

All scripts are in /sandbox. The ones to reuse are /sandbox/probe_vis_lib.py (env wrapper with goto, turn and selectors), /sandbox/probe_vis_model.py (slab-test helpers) and /sandbox/probe_vis_fit3.py (the occlusion model fit). The pillar-sweep data is in /sandbox/probe_vis_d1.json, /sandbox/probe_vis_j_*.json and /sandbox/probe_vis_n_*.json.
````

import sys, time
import numpy as np
from env_client import make_env
from approach import GeneratedApproach
def run(seed, verbose=False):
    env = make_env()
    obs, info = env.reset(seed=seed)
    ap = GeneratedApproach(env.action_space, env.observation_space, {})
    t0=time.time(); ap.reset(obs, info); tp=time.time()-t0
    steps=0; term=False
    while steps < env.max_steps:
        a = ap.get_action(obs)
        obs, r, term, trunc, info = env.step(a)
        steps += 1
        if term or trunc: break

"""
new="""        for ri in range(2):
            P = tabs[ri][0]
            self.actions[ri] = self._extract(P, best[1][ri][1])
        # time-aware re-plan of final send against other rover's trajectory
        trajs = []
        for ri in range(2):
            r = sc.rovers["rover%d" % ri]
            trajs.append([(r["x"], r["y"])] + [(a[0], a[1]) for a in self.actions[ri]])
        new_actions = list(self.actions)
        for ri in range(2):
            stages = best[1][ri][1]
            if stages[-1][0] != "send":
                continue
            P = tabs[ri][0]
            Fprev = stages[-2][3]
            G0 = op_stage(Fprev, P.land)
            other = trajs[1 - ri]
            G = np.full(G0.shape, INF, dtype=G0.dtype)
            pending_mask = G0 < INF
            tmin = int(G0[pending_mask].min()) if pending_mask.any() else INF
            lx, ly = sc.lander
            t = tmin
            while pending_mask.any() and t < tmin + 200:
                ox, oy = other[min(t, len(other) - 1)]
                blk = seg_hits_disk(P.X, P.Y, lx, ly, ox, oy, ROVER_OCC_R) | \\
                    seg_hits_disk(P.camx, P.camy, lx, ly, ox, oy, ROVER_OCC_R)
                ok = pending_mask & (G0 <= t) & ~blk
                G[ok] = t
                pending_mask &= ~ok
                if t >= len(other) - 1 and not ok.any() and (G0 <= t).all():
                    break
                t += 1
            F2 = propagate(G, P.free)
            if F2[(P.hi, P.hj)] >= INF:
                continue
            st = stages[:-1] + [("send", None, G, F2)]
            new_actions[ri] = self._extract(P, st)
        self.actions = new_actions
"""
s=s.replace(old,new)
open('approach.py','w').write(s)
EOF

from concurrent.futures import ThreadPoolExecutor
def f(seed):

cat > probe_occ_lib.py <<'EOF'
from probe_send_lib import E, SEL
import numpy as np, math, time
def setup(seed, P0, th0, Q, h1, wp1=()):
    e=E(seed)
    # rover1 to Q via waypoints
    for w in list(wp1)+[Q]:
        if not e.goto(1,*w,tol=1e-4,maxit=100): return e,'r1 blocked at %s'%(e.pose(1),)
    e.turn(1,h1)
    # rover0 sample
    if not e.goto(0,1.28,-0.95+0.0,tol=1e-3): return e,'r0 blocked to sample'
    e.act(0,(0,0,0),SEL['sample'])
    if e.g('rover0','store_full')<0.5: return e,'sample failed'
    if not e.goto(0,*P0,tol=1e-4): return e,'r0 blocked to P0 %s'%(e.pose(0),)
    e.turn(0,th0)
    return e,None
def sweep(seed,P0,th0,Q,h1,d,step=0.004,n=60,wp1=()):
    e,err=setup(seed,P0,th0,Q,h1,wp1)
    if err: return dict(err=err)
    p0=e.pose(0); hist=[]
    for i in range(n):
        before=e.pose(1)
        mv=(d[0]*step,d[1]*step,0) if i>0 else (0,0,0)
        e.step((0,0,0,SEL['send']),mv+(0,))
        p1=e.pose(1)
        if i>0 and abs(p1[0]-before[0])+abs(p1[1]-before[1])<1e-7: return dict(err='r1 stuck',p0=p0,p1=p1)
        if e.g('rover0','store_full')<0.5:
            return dict(i=i,p0=p0,p1=p1,prev=before if i>0 else None)
    return dict(i=None,p0=p0,p1=e.pose(1))
EOF

EOF

    x,y,th=p0; c,s=math.cos(th),math.sin(th); return (x+c*-0.087-s*-0.0125, y+s*-0.087+c*-0.0125)
L=(-1.9,-2.0)
for name,src in [('centre',lambda p:p[:2]),('cam',cam)]:
    print(name)
    for p0,b,h,d in recs:
        dist,sg=segd(b,src(p0),L); print('  ',p0[:2],b,h,d,round(dist*sg,4))

    def _realize(self, sc, tabs, costs):
        best = (None, costs)
        actions = [[], []]
        for ri in range(2):
            P = tabs[ri][0]
            actions[ri] = self._extract(P, best[1][ri][1])
        # time-aware re-plan of final send against other rover's trajectory
        trajs = []
        for ri in range(2):
            r = sc.rovers["rover%d" % ri]
            trajs.append([(r["x"], r["y"])] + [(a[0], a[1]) for a in actions[ri]])
        new_actions = list(actions)
        for ri in range(2):
            stages = best[1][ri][1]
            if stages[-1][0] != "send":
                continue
            P = tabs[ri][0]
            Fprev = stages[-2][3]
            G0 = op_stage(Fprev, P.land)
            other = trajs[1 - ri]
            G = np.full(G0.shape, INF, dtype=G0.dtype)
            pending_mask = G0 < INF
            tmin = int(G0[pending_mask].min()) if pending_mask.any() else INF
            lx, ly = sc.lander
            t = tmin
            while pending_mask.any() and t < tmin + 200:
                ox, oy = other[min(t, len(other) - 1)]
                blk = seg_hits_disk(P.X, P.Y, lx, ly, ox, oy, ROVER_OCC_R) | \
                    seg_hits_disk(P.camx, P.camy, lx, ly, ox, oy, ROVER_OCC_R)
                ok = pending_mask & (G0 <= t) & ~blk
                G[ok] = t
                pending_mask &= ~ok
                if t >= len(other) - 1 and not ok.any() and (G0 <= t).all():
                    break
                t += 1
            F2 = propagate(G, P.free)
            if F2[(P.hi, P.hj)] >= INF:
                continue
            st = stages[:-1] + [("send_t", None, G, F2)]
            new_actions[ri] = self._extract(P, st)
        return new_actions

    def _extract(self, P, stages):

from probe_occ_lib import *
from concurrent.futures import ThreadPoolExecutor
import sys
L=np.array((-1.9,-2.0))
def camp(P0,th=math.pi):
    c,s=math.cos(th),math.sin(th); return np.array((P0[0]-0.087*c+0.0125*s, P0[1]-0.087*s-0.0125*c))
def point(P0,x,sd):
    C=camp(P0); d=L-C; d/=np.linalg.norm(d); n=np.array((-d[1],d[0]))  # cross(d,n)>0
    t=(x-C[0])/(L[0]-C[0]); base=C+t*(L-C)
    q=base+sd*n
    # sign convention: cross(L-C, q-C) = sd*|..| >0 -> check
    return (round(float(q[0]),4),round(float(q[1]),4))
def test(job):
    P0,x,sd,h=job; Q=point(P0,x,sd)
    e,err=setup(44,P0,math.pi,Q,h)
    if err: e.env.close(); return job,Q,err
    e.step((0,0,0,SEL['send']),(0,0,0,0)); ok=e.feats('sample5')[6]>0.5; e.env.close()
    return job,Q,int(ok)
if __name__=='__main__':
    P=(0.6,-0.35); jobs=[]
    jobs+=[(P,-0.3,round(s,3),math.pi/4) for s in np.arange(0.03,0.26,0.02)]
    jobs+=[(P,-0.6,round(-s,3),math.pi/4) for s in np.arange(0.05,0.26,0.02)]
    jobs+=[(P,-0.45,round(s,3),0.0) for s in np.arange(-0.25,0.26,0.025)]
    jobs+=[(P,-1.0,round(sg*s,3),0.0) for s in np.arange(0.15,0.26,0.02) for sg in (1,-1)]
    with ThreadPoolExecutor(12) as ex:
        for r in ex.map(test,jobs): print(r,flush=True)
EOF

### E0852 · Message

Source line 852; turn 1; start line not saved/not applicable.

[Previous](#E0851) · [Next](#E0855)

Actor: helper: Probe rover occlusion of send. Parent tool: `toolu_01AABTpX1nno6kRVcm5SpA5r`. Timestamp: 2026-10-01T09:24:07.048Z.

Exact agent message:
```text
The best fit is a 2D segment from rover0's camera point to the lander centre, with rover1 treated as a disc around its centre. Blocking reached up to about 0.23 from that segment, so the conservative model below uses r = 0.25. The real occluder isn't a clean disc: it has gaps and depends on rover1's heading, which looks like a 3D raycast against rover1's body (wheels, chassis, mast). I didn't model that 3D shape; this is a fit to measured blocked/free positions.

**Method.** All runs used seed 44, which has no pillars in the lower-middle region. Rover0 picked up sample5 at (1.28,-0.95), moved to a test pose with heading pi, then sent every step while rover1 moved in 0.005 steps away from the line. A failed send costs nothing, so each episode ends at its first success. I ran 5 rover0/rover1 geometries and 8 rover1 headings (about 70 episodes), plus about 55 single-point episodes to look for gaps. Distances below are perpendicular distances to the cam→lander-centre segment, where cam = (x,y)+R(θ)(-0.087,-0.0125).

**Findings**
- **Ray endpoints:** with rover1 near the lander (x=-1.2, -1.0, -0.8) the blocked band is symmetric about the cam→lander-centre segment for every heading: ±0.181 (within ±0.003). The centre-to-centre segment gives a lopsided band (-0.165/+0.194 and -0.169/+0.190). So the ray starts at rover0's camera point and ends at the lander centre.
- **Near the lander:** rover1 acts like a disc of radius about 0.18 that doesn't depend on heading (identical flip points for headings 0, ±pi/2, pi). It was blocked at 0.15 and 0.17 and free from 0.19 outward.
- **Nearer rover0 (rover1 x > -0.8):** the shape depends on heading and has gaps.
  - At x=-0.45, heading 0: free at 0 to ±0.075, blocked at ±0.10, free at ±0.125, blocked at ±0.15, free from ±0.175 outward.
  - The furthest blocked distances seen were 0.2304 (x=-0.38, heading pi/2), 0.2285 (x=-0.8, heading 0), and 0.220–0.223 in a few other heading-0/pi cases near rover0, all on the upper (+y) side. On the lower side the maximum was 0.206.
- **Your earlier observation doesn't reproduce.** In seed 44, rover0 at (0.6,-0.35) heading pi sent successfully with rover1 at home (-1.0,-1.75) heading 0. That spot is 0.276 from the cam→lander-centre segment, outside every blocked distance I measured. The earlier failure was probably caused by something else in that episode, such as a pillar or a different rover0 pose.
- **Correction for NOTES.md: send detection.** A successful send does NOT clear `store_full`; it stays 1. Success shows only as the item's received flag (the sample's 7th feature, index 6), and the env returns reward -1.0 that step. I didn't edit NOTES.md, as instructed.

**Recommended conservative model:** the send is blocked by rover1 if `dist(rover1_xy, segment(cam0, (-1.9,-2.0))) < 0.25`. Use 0.24 if you need it tighter; 0.25 leaves about 0.02 margin over the largest observed value. Ignore rover1's heading and treat the gaps as blocked. Keep the existing range check (camera point to lander ≤ 4.0) and the pillar checks alongside it.

**Files** (all in /sandbox):
- `probe_occ_lib.py`: setup and sweep helpers.
- `probe_occ_pt.py`: single-point tests.
- `probe_occ_fit.py`: computes signed distances.
- `probe_occ_run*.out`, `probe_occ_pt.out`: raw results.
```

import sys, json
import numpy as np
from env_client import make_env
import approach
from concurrent.futures import ThreadPoolExecutor
def f(seed):
    env=make_env(); obs,info=env.reset(seed=seed); env.close()

    ap=approach.GeneratedApproach(None,None,{}); ap.reset(obs,info)
    a=max(len(x) for x in ap.actions)

    ap=approach.GeneratedApproach(None,None,{}); ap.reset(obs,info)
    return seed, a, max(len(x) for x in ap.actions)

print("gaps", [(s,a,b) for s,a,b in out if a!=b])
EOF

cat >> NOTES.md <<'EOF'
## Later findings
- Rovers are updated sequentially within a step: rover0 move+op, then rover1 move+op. So rover0's send sees rover1's PREVIOUS position.
- Rover occluder for send LOS: disk ~0.23 around rover centre vs segment cam->lander centre (use 0.26).
- Lander send range measured from cam point too.
- Image picks nearest objective (liberal: any within range) not yet imaged by this rover -> planner excludes cells where another un-imaged objective is nearer.
- Sample picks nearest sample -> region requires target type strictly nearest.
- Facing -y (theta=-pi/2) while imaging moves cam 0.087 toward objectives: ~0.7 steps saved.
- Max objectives = 4 (4 mounds).
## Approach (approach.py)
- Per-rover coarse grid (0.05) staged BFS over task orders (DFS trie), joint assignment min makespan,
  top-K realised on fine grid (0.025) with time-aware send vs other rover trajectory; replan on deviation.
- Results: seeds 0-400 all solved, mean 20.475 steps.
EOF

The wall and mounds don't occlude.\n     - Calibration persists across moves until a successful image. Calibrate needs any objective visible.\n     - Image takes the nearest visible objective this rover hasn't imaged.\n   - **Send:** the lander is at (-1.9,-2.0); range ≤ 4.0 from both the centre and the cam point. Pillars occlude. The other rover occludes as a disk of ~0.23 around the cam→lander segment. The wall does NOT block. One send transfers everything held.\n   - **Sample:** range < 0.25 (0.245 works). It takes the nearest sample. Samples persist after sampling.\n   - **Termination:** terminated=True when the goal holds: one stone and one soil received, all images received, both rovers at home, both stores empty.\n     - at_home means distance < 0.25 and heading within ~0.4.\n     - The env has no truncation.\n   - **Max objectives** is 4 (4 mounds). `reset(seed, options={\"object_count\": n})` pins the count.\n   - **Planner design:**\n     - Per-rover grid aligned to the home position (coarse RES 0.05, WIN 4).\n     - Staged BFS: `op_stage` is minimum_filter + 1 masked to the region; `propagate` iterates a min-filter.\n     - A DFS trie over task orders (objectives as cal+img, stone/soil as sample+drop, then send) produces a table mapping task set → cost.\n     - Joint assignment minimises (makespan, sum).\n     - The top-6 candidates are realised: refined on a fine grid (0.025), with a time-aware send stage checked against the other rover's trajectory at t-1 and t, then backtracked (waiting allowed) and given a heading schedule.\n     - Imaging heading is -π/2. The schedule rotates 0.4 rad/step, with cal/img at times ≥ nrot_in, and waits appended so the rover can rotate back.\n     - Home region radius is 0.235.\n     - Execution replans when a deviation is detected: wrong position or heading, or an op with no effect. Attributes:\n       - `ctor`, `free`, `home_reg`\n       - cam points `camx/camy` (home heading) and `camx_i/camy_i` (imaging heading)\n       - `vis[k]`, `objd[k]`, `any_vis`\n       - `land` (intersection over the rotation headings, with static occluders for the other rover's home and current position) and `land_free` (without the rover occluders)\n       - `sreg[kind]` (target type strictly nearest)\n       - `img_region(k, imaged)` (excludes cells where an un-imaged competitor is within 2.03 and nearer than dk + 0.03)\n       - `nrot_in`, `nrot_out`, `cell_of`\n     - `GeneratedApproach` methods:\n       - `reset`: sets homes, replans, expect, prev_sc, log, bad, t_start, then calls `_plan`.\n       - `_rover_tables`: computes occl and a single ths entry, then calls `_rover_tables_h`. Table entries are (cost, stages, P).\n       - `_plan`: computes needs and pending, enumerates assignments into cands, realises the top-6, and handles the RELAX fallback. Sets `self.pred` and `self.actions`.\n       - `_refine`: fine grid with cache `self._fine_cache`.\n       - `_realize`: timed \"send_t\" stage, then `_schedule`.\n       - `_extract`: backtrack with modes for exact vs ≤ predecessor.\n       - `_schedule`: returns (x, y, op, heading) tuples.\n       - `get_action`: replans on deviation or empty actions; sets dx/dy clipped, dθ, selector.\n       - `_deviated`: checks position, heading, cal, img target, sample type, drop and send success; logs into `self.log` and appends rejected move targets to `self.bad`.\n   - **test_approach.py:** `run(seed)` returns (seed, count, term, steps, replans, plan_time, total_time). It runs seeds with an 8-thread pool and dumps JSON to argv[3].\n   - **Other test scripts:**\n     - test_alt.py: runs with the APPROACH env var.\n     - test_cnt.py: pinned object_count.\n     - dbg.py: prints pred and log for seeds.\n     - dbg2–dbg9, timeit_.py (profiling), bound.py, bound2.py.\n   - **NOTES.md:** all probed facts, the approach summary and results.\n   - Probe scripts from subagents: probe_col_*, probe_send_*, probe_vis_*, probe_occ_*.\n\n4. Errors and fixes:\n   - A sample spot was in range of both stone and soil, so the env sampled the nearer, wrong one. Fixed by making the target type strictly nearest (other type > 0.26 away or 0.03 farther) and checking the analysed type on deviation.\n   - Image photographed a different objective because my conservative visibility missed a nearer one. Fixed with a liberal competitor test.\n   - Send failed when the lander was out of range measured from the cam point. Fixed by checking range from both the cam and the centre.\n   - Send was blocked by the other rover mid-trajectory. Fixed with the time-aware send stage. The blocking rover's position turned out to be the previous step's because of sequential updates, so I check both t-1 and t.\n   - The backtracker failed with waits, giving a truncated plan and a replan loop on seed 103. Rewrote `_extract` to allow ≤ predecessors (waiting).\n   - Rotation was rejected near the lander (seed 59 infinite loop). Made the lander rule conservative and added the blacklist of rejected targets.\n   - A negative-inflation hack in bound.py was invalid; switched to monkeypatching seg_hits_box.\n   - Experiments that were reverted: mixing imaging headings (no gain, slower) and a 1.2 rad rotation (worse).\n\n5. Problem Solving / Results:\n   - Seeds 0–400: 400/400 solved, mean 20.475 steps, 0 replans.\n   - 4-objective test: 60/60, mean 21.8.\n   - Seeds 400–600: 199/200, mean 20.16. **Seed 549 fails.** Rover0's send fails repeatedly at (1.15,-1.6), (0.95,-1.8) and (0.775,-1.8) with heading -π (back at home heading, holding images). The replan keeps choosing send spots that fail, causing 987 replans and a 60s timeout.\n   - Probable cause: an unmodelled occlusion near the rover0 home area, e.g. rover1 parked at home blocking with a larger footprint, or a pillar close to the line. The blacklist only handles move failures, not send failures.\n   - Single-thread planning takes about 2–4s; under 8-thread contention it reaches ~18–23s.\n\n6. All user messages:\n   - The initial task description (the full Rovers environment spec and instructions summarised in section 1), including:\n     - \"IMPORTANT: You MUST write ALL files ... using RELATIVE paths only.\"\n     - \"approach.py itself must NOT import env_client.\"\n     - \"Write code often to approach.py ... make sure that approach.py is your best current attempt at all times.\"\n     - The commit instructions.\n     - CLAUDE.md context-management rules.\n   - No other user messages. The system reminders were only \"keep the user updated\".\n\n7. Pending Tasks:\n   - Fix the seed 549 failure: repeated send failure, then a replan loop.\n   - Keep approach.py as the best version and commit after changes.\n\n8. Current Work:\n   I was debugging seed 549 with `dbg.py 549`. The log shows repeated deviations of the form `('dev', 0, (0.775, -1.8, ('send', None), -3.14159...), ..., [False, False])`. Rover0 holds images and fails to send from positions near its home while (presumably) rover1 is at home or nearby. The last committed approach.py includes the RELAX fallback and object-name parsing.\n\n9. Optional Next Step:\n   - Diagnose seed 549. Print the pillars and rover1's position at the failure and check the line from rover0's cam to the lander (-1.9,-2.0).\n   - Then add robustness for repeated send failures, for example:\n     - record failed send positions (plus the other rover's position) into a blacklist or occluder list used when building `P.land` / `land_free` in replans, or\n     - after a failed send, add the other rover's current *and* previous positions as occluders with a larger radius and forbid that send cell, so the replan picks a different send spot.\n   - Re-run `test_approach.py 400 600 res_final.json` (and 0–400) to confirm no regressions, then commit.\n\nIf you need specific details from before compaction (like exact code snippets, error messages, or content you generated), read the full transcript at: /home/node/.claude/projects/-sandbox/4f61efab-6317-47d3-a459-35e1677f1fdb.jsonl\nContinue the conversation from where it left off without asking the user any further questions. def seg_hits_box(px, py, qx, qy, cx, cy, hx, hy):
    """Vectorised: does segment p->q (p arrays, q scalar) intersect AABB?"""
    if RELAX[0]:
        return np.zeros(np.shape(px), dtype=bool)
    dx = qx - px
    dy = qy - py
    t0 = np.zeros_like(px)
    t1 = np.ones_like(px)
    ok = np.ones(px.shape, dtype=bool)
    for d, p, lo, hi in ((dx, px, cx - hx, cx + hx), (dy, py, cy - hy, cy + hy)):
        small = np.abs(d) < 1e-12
        ok &= ~(small & ((p < lo) | (p > hi)))
        with np.errstate(divide="ignore", invalid="ignore"):
            ta = (lo - p) / d
            tb = (hi - p) / d
        tmin = np.where(small, -np.inf, np.minimum(ta, tb))
        tmax = np.where(small, np.inf, np.maximum(ta, tb))
        t0 = np.maximum(t0, tmin)
        t1 = np.minimum(t1, tmax)
    return ok & (t0 <= t1)


def seg_hits_disk(px, py, qx, qy, cx, cy, r):
    dx = qx - px
```

cat >> NOTES.md <<'EOF'

## Sample markers near lander (seeds 549, 706)
- Samples lying within ~0.05 of the lander can occlude sends in strange bearing ranges (probably a 3D raycast). This is rare (~2/800 seeds have a sample within 0.05).
- Model: each sample is a box (half 0.045) occluding the ray cam->lander, with the ray trimmed at the lander box (half 0.06). This fixed 549 but did not predict 706.
- Robustness: failed send/img/cal positions are added to self.bad as (x,y,op,arg). The planner then excludes land/vis/any_vis within 0.08 of them, so a replan won't retry the same spot. 706 is now solved in 32 steps, with 2 replans.
- Results: seeds 400-600 200/200 (mean 20.185); 600-800 200/200 (mean 20.57). Single-thread worst plan time ~7s.
EOF
git add -A; git commit -qm "notes

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>"; echo ok

import sys, time
import numpy as np
from env_client import make_env
from approach import GeneratedApproach
cnt=int(sys.argv[1])
def run(seed):
    env = make_env()
    try:
        obs, info = env.reset(seed=seed, options={"object_count": cnt})
    except Exception as e:
        return seed, 'err', str(e)[:100]
    n=len([o for o in obs if o.type.name=='objective'])
    ap = GeneratedApproach(env.action_space, env.observation_space, {})
    t0=time.time(); ap.reset(obs, info); tp=time.time()-t0
    steps=0
    while steps < 300:
        obs, r, term, trunc, info = env.step(ap.get_action(obs)); steps+=1
        if term: break
    env.close()
    return seed, n, term, steps, ap.replans, round(tp,2), round(time.time()-t0,1)
from concurrent.futures import ThreadPoolExecutor
with ThreadPoolExecutor(8) as ex: res=list(ex.map(run, range(int(sys.argv[2]), int(sys.argv[3]))))
for r in res:
    if len(r)<5 or not r[2] or r[4]: print(r)
ok=[r for r in res if r[2] is True]
print('solved',len(ok),len(res),'mean',np.mean([r[3] for r in ok]),'maxplan',max(r[5] for r in ok))
```

<a id="E1514"></a>
### E1514 · Message

Source line 1514; turn 1; start line not saved/not applicable.

[Previous](#E1513) · [Next](#E1515)

Actor: main stream. Parent tool: `none`. Timestamp: 2026-10-01T11:34:14.580Z.

Exact agent message:
```text
I fixed the one failing instance (seed 549). Across the 700 instances re-run with the final `approach.py`, every one now finishes, with no timeouts, and it's committed.

**What was wrong with seed 549:** a sample marker lies almost on top of the lander and blocks some sight lines to it. Rover0's send to the lander kept failing, the planner kept choosing send spots that also failed, and it hit the 60s limit after 987 replans.

**What I changed:**
- **Sample markers can block sends.** The planner now treats sample markers as obstacles between the rover and the lander. My model of their shape is a rough fit: it fixed seed 549 but didn't predict the failures on seed 706, the only other case seen. Samples this close to the lander are rare (2 of the 800 seeds I checked).
- **Failed spots are remembered.** If a send, image or calibrate fails at a position, the replanner won't use that spot again. Seed 706 now recovers this way, but costs 10 extra steps (32 instead of the planned 22).

**Results with the final version:**

| Instances | Solved | Mean steps |
|---|---|---|
| Seeds 0–200 | 200/200 | 20.74 (one seed is a step worse than before) |
| Seeds 400–600 | 200/200 | 20.185 (was 199/200) |
| Seeds 600–800 | 200/200 | 20.57 (only seed 706 needed replans) |
| Seeds 100–200 with 4 objectives | 100/100 | 21.95 |

Seeds 200–400 weren't re-run after this change; they were all solved before it.

**Time budget:** planning takes about 5–7s when run alone. With 8 tests running in parallel it reached 56s on a 4-objective instance, close to the 60s limit. If evaluation runs instances in parallel on a slower machine, that could matter. The existing time guards cut back planning after 20s.

**Not adopted:** I tried giving pillars a smaller safety margin. On seeds 400–600 it improved the mean only from 20.185 to 20.16 steps and adds collision risk, so I kept the safer values.

Findings and results are recorded in `NOTES.md`.
```

    "result": "I fixed the one failing instance (seed 549). Across the 700 instances re-run with the final `approach.py`, every one now finishes, with no timeouts, and it's committed.\n\n**What was wrong with seed 549:** a sample marker lies almost on top of the lander and blocks some sight lines to it. Rover0's send to the lander kept failing, the planner kept choosing send spots that also failed, and it hit the 60s limit after 987 replans.\n\n**What I changed:**\n- **Sample markers can block sends.** The planner now treats sample markers as obstacles between the rover and the lander. My model of their shape is a rough fit: it fixed seed 549 but didn't predict the failures on seed 706, the only other case seen. Samples this close to the lander are rare (2 of the 800 seeds I checked).\n- **Failed spots are remembered.** If a send, image or calibrate fails at a position, the replanner won't use that spot again. Seed 706 now recovers this way, but costs 10 extra steps (32 instead of the planned 22).\n\n**Results with the final version:**\n\n| Instances | Solved | Mean steps |\n|---|---|---|\n| Seeds 0–200 | 200/200 | 20.74 (one seed is a step worse than before) |\n| Seeds 400–600 | 200/200 | 20.185 (was 199/200) |\n| Seeds 600–800 | 200/200 | 20.57 (only seed 706 needed replans) |\n| Seeds 100–200 with 4 objectives | 100/100 | 21.95 |\n\nSeeds 200–400 weren't re-run after this change; they were all solved before it.\n\n**Time budget:** planning takes about 5–7s when run alone. With 8 tests running in parallel it reached 56s on a 4-objective instance, close to the 60s limit. If evaluation runs instances in parallel on a slower machine, that could matter. The existing time guards cut back planning after 20s.\n\n**Not adopted:** I tried giving pillars a smaller safety margin. On seeds 400–600 it improved the mean only from 20.185 to 20.16 steps and adds collision risk, so I kept the safer values.\n\nFindings and results are recorded in `NOTES.md`.",
